commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Renamed Duke to GLaDOS, added greet-and-exit statement
Add support for echoing user commands
Add support for storing and listing tasks
Add present-changes-visually skill
Add support for marking tasks as done
Add support for unmarking tasks
Add Task class to represent tasks
Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Java code in this project follows no written standard, so style
decisions vary between increments.

Let's capture the SE-EDU Java coding standard as a project skill so the
same rules apply to all future code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Commit messages in this project follow no written convention.

Let's capture the SE-EDU Git conventions as a project skill so commit
messages can be checked against a single reference.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Mandate SE-EDU Java and Git standards
Tweak code to follow the Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Neither class has a header comment, and the command keywords and
substring offsets appear as literals in the command loop.

Let's add Javadoc to both classes and their public methods, and move
the command keywords, task limit, and output formatting into named
constants.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for todo, deadline, and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list could only store plain descriptions, with no way to
attach a due date or a start/end time to a task.

Let's add a Task constructor that accepts an optional due date and
start/end time, and three new commands in the command loop to create
todo, deadline, and event tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use inheritance for todo, deadline, and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Task carried a type marker plus fields for every task type, and each
constructor call had to pass null for whichever fields did not apply.

Let's make Todo, Deadline, and Event separate classes that extend
Task, each holding only the fields it actually needs, and store them
polymorphically in a Task array.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Compiles the program, feeds each recorded input to it, and compares
the full console output against what test/ui-test-plan.md expects.

commitResults.messageTitle: Agents.md: Require test-ui after UI-affecting changes
Extract the task-added confirmation into a method
commitResults.messageBody:
The "Got it. I've added this task:" confirmation was written out as
the same three println calls in the todo, deadline, and event
branches, so any change to that message would need editing in three
places and risk them drifting apart.

Let's extract that block into printTaskAdded, called once from each
of the three branches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract deadline and event parsing out of main
commitResults.messageBody:
main mixed high-level command dispatch with the low-level detail of
locating delimiters and slicing substrings for deadline and event
input, so a reader following the command loop had to also follow
string-parsing arithmetic along the way.

Let's move that parsing into parseDeadline and parseEvent, so main
stays at one level: read a command, hand it off, print the reply.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract shared task-index parsing for mark and unmark
commitResults.messageBody:
The mark and unmark branches each parsed the task number with the
same expression, differing only in which command constant was used
to find where the number starts.

Let's extract that into parseTaskIndex, taking the command prefix as
a parameter so both branches share one parsing implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Consolidate task-adding into a single addTask method
commitResults.messageBody:
The todo, deadline, and event branches each stored a task, incremented
taskCount, and printed the same confirmation, differing only in what
was constructed.

Let's extract that into addTask, which returns the updated count since
Java passes taskCount by value and the increment can't otherwise be
seen by main.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle todo commands with no description
commitResults.messageBody:
A bare "todo" does not match COMMAND_TODO, which requires a trailing
space, so it falls through every branch and is silently ignored. A
"todo " with nothing after it creates a task with a blank description.

Let's treat "todo" as a command word matched either alone or followed
by arguments, and print an error message when the description is empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unrecognised commands with an error message
commitResults.messageBody:
Input matching none of the known commands falls through the whole
dispatch chain, so the user sees an empty response block with no
indication that anything went wrong.

Let's add a final else branch that prints an error listing the
commands that are actually available, so the user can correct the
mistake without guessing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate mark and unmark arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
The task number after mark or unmark is passed straight to
Integer.parseInt and used as an array index, so a non-numeric or
out-of-range argument crashes the program. A bare "mark" does not
match the command at all and is reported as an unknown command.

Let's match mark and unmark as command words, then check the argument
is present, numeric, and within range, printing a specific message
for each case and skipping the mark/unmark when one fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate deadline and event input
commitResults.messageBody:
The delimiters require a space on both sides and their positions are
used as substring bounds without checking, so a deadline or event
missing /by, /from or /to crashes the program, as does a /to placed
before its /from.

Let's match both as command words, search for the delimiters without
requiring surrounding spaces, and print a message naming the expected
format when a delimiter or either part around it is missing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-5'
Use a custom exception to report command errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Each validation prints its own error and signals failure differently,
returning -1 from parseTaskIndex and null from parseDeadline and
parseEvent, so every caller needs a guard clause before acting on the
result, and the printing is scattered across five places.

Let's add a GLaDOSException class, throw it from each validation, and
catch it once around the command dispatch, so failures cannot fall
through to the happy path and all error output goes through one place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Exceptions'
Organise classes into packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All six classes sit in the default package at the source root, so
there is nothing grouping the task hierarchy separately from the
chatbot's entry point and error type.

Let's move GLaDOS and GLaDOSException into a glados package and the
four task classes into glados.task, and point the test-ui runner at
the nested sources and the fully qualified main class.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages'
Store tasks in an ArrayList instead of a fixed array
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are kept in a Task[] of size 100 alongside a separate taskCount
that every add has to return and reassign.

The upcoming delete command would have to shift array elements by hand
and keep taskCount in sync, which is error-prone.

Let's replace the array and counter with an ArrayList<Task>.

ArrayList resizes itself, tracks its own size, and supports removing an
element by index, so the list has no hard limit and addTask no longer
needs to pass a count back.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a delete command to remove tasks from the list
commitResults.messageBody:
Once added, a task stays in the list for good; the only way to get rid
of a finished or mistaken task is to restart the program.

Let's add "delete N", which removes task N and reports the task removed
and how many remain.

It reuses parseTaskIndex, so a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range
number is rejected with the same messages as mark and unmark.

commitResults.messageTitle: test-ui: Run each test in a fresh folder and support data file checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The test runner starts GLaDOS in the repository root, and can only
compare console output.

Once GLaDOS saves its task list to data/glados.txt, tests would write
that file into the repository, and a later test would start with the
tasks left by an earlier one. There is also no way to check what was
saved, or to set up a saved file to test loading.

Let's run each test in its own empty temporary folder, and support
optional "Data file before" and "Data file after" blocks in the plan.

A fresh folder per test keeps tests independent of each other and of
whatever data a developer has saved locally.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save the task list to a file whenever it changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks exist only in memory, so every task is lost when GLaDOS exits.

Let's write the whole list to data/glados.txt after every add, mark,
and unmark, one task per line, e.g. "D | 0 | return book | Sunday".

Each task class formats its own line via toFileString(), so a new task
type only needs to override that method. A Storage class holds the
file handling so GLaDOS does not deal with file I/O directly. The path
is relative and built with Path.of, so it works from any project folder
on any OS, and the data folder is created if it does not exist yet.
The data folder is git-ignored since it holds local user data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks from the data file at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are saved to data/glados.txt after every change, but GLaDOS
always starts with an empty list, so saved tasks never come back.

Let's read the data file at startup and rebuild each task from its
line, including its done status.

When the file does not exist yet, as on a first run, the list simply
starts empty. If the file exists but cannot be read, GLaDOS reports it
and starts empty rather than failing to start.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle corrupted data files and reserved characters in tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading assumes every line of the data file is well formed. A line
with an unknown type, missing fields, or a bad done flag either crashes
GLaDOS at startup or loads as the wrong task. Separately, a task whose
text contains "|" is saved in a form that cannot be read back.

Let's validate each line while loading, skip and count the ones that
are malformed, and warn the user at startup when any were skipped.
Let's also reject "|" in todo, deadline, and event input.

Skipping bad lines keeps the rest of the user's tasks usable instead of
refusing to start. Rejecting "|" at input is simpler and safer than
escaping it in the file format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-6'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
Extract Ui class to handle user interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
GLaDOS reads input and prints every reply itself, so the command logic
is mixed with formatting details such as the indent, divider lines,
and banner.

Keeping both in one class makes the command loop harder to follow,
and any change to how replies look means editing code spread across
the whole loop.

Let's move all input reading and reply printing into a new Ui class,
with one method per kind of reply.

GLaDOS now only decides what happens, and Ui decides how it looks, so
formatting changes stay in one place. Console output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class to hold the task list
commitResults.messageBody:
GLaDOS, Ui, and Storage each work on a raw ArrayList<Task>, and GLaDOS
calls ArrayList methods such as remove directly.

Every class that touches the list depends on how it is stored, so
changing the storage, or adding list operations such as find, means
editing code in several places.

Let's wrap the list in a new TaskList class with add, delete, get, and
size, and pass a TaskList around instead of the ArrayList.

Other classes now only use those operations, so how the tasks are
stored is decided in TaskList alone. Storage.load still returns an
ArrayList, which GLaDOS wraps in a TaskList, matching the suggested
design. Console output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class to make sense of commands
commitResults.messageBody:
GLaDOS works out which command was entered and parses its arguments
itself, so the command loop sits among the command words, delimiters,
and parsing helpers.

Mixing these makes the loop harder to follow, and changing a command's
format means editing the same class that runs the conversation.

Let's move the command words, delimiters, and parsing methods into a
new Parser class, and add parseCommandWord to work out which command
was entered, rejecting unknown ones.

GLaDOS now only decides what each command does. Parser methods are
static since they keep no state, and the command word constants are
public so GLaDOS can compare against them. Console output is
unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Copy the list given to the constructor
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList keeps a reference to the ArrayList it is created with, so any
other code holding that list could change the tasks without going
through TaskList.

Let's copy the given tasks into a new list, so TaskList alone controls
its contents.

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn GLaDOS into an object with a run method
commitResults.messageBody:
GLaDOS does all its work inside the static main method, which creates
the Ui, Storage, and TaskList as local variables and passes them to
helper methods such as addTask.

Passing the same objects around adds noise to every helper, and main
mixes setting up the chatbot with running the conversation.

Let's keep Ui, Storage, and TaskList as fields, set them up in a
constructor, move the conversation into run(), and reduce main to
creating a GLaDOS and running it. The body of the command loop moves
into handleCommand, and addTask now also saves the list.

Tasks are loaded in run() after the welcome, not in the constructor,
so any loading warning still appears below the welcome message.
Console output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreOOP'
Store deadline due dates as dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
A deadline keeps its /by as plain text, so GLaDOS cannot tell that
"2/12/2019 1800" means 2 December 2019, 6pm, and accepts anything,
such as "Sunday", as a due date.

Let's add a TaskDateTime class that holds a date with an optional time,
and store a deadline's due date in it. The /by is accepted as
yyyy-mm-dd or d/m/yyyy, each optionally followed by a 24-hour time, and
is shown as e.g. "Oct 15 2019" or "Dec 02 2019 6:00 PM".

The time is optional because many deadlines only have a date, and
showing "12:00 AM" for those would be misleading. Strict parsing
rejects dates that do not exist, such as 2019-02-30. The data file
saves dates as e.g. "2019-12-02 1800", so they stay easy to edit, and
lines with an unreadable date are skipped as corrupted. Month names are
always printed in English, so output is the same on any computer.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store event start and end as dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
An event keeps its /from and /to as plain text, while a deadline now
understands dates. The two task types behave differently, and an event
can end before it starts without GLaDOS noticing.

Let's store an event's start and end as TaskDateTime values, accepted
in the same forms as a deadline's /by, and reject an event that ends
before it starts, both when it is entered and when it is loaded.

When either end has no time, only the dates are compared, so a date
with no time counts as the whole day. This lets an event that starts
at 1800 end on the same date without a time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add on command to list the tasks on a date
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines and events now hold real dates, but the only way to see what
falls on a given day is to read the whole list and work it out by hand.

Let's add "on DATE", e.g. "on 2019-10-15", which lists the deadlines
due that day and the events running across it.

Each task class decides whether it falls on a date by overriding
occursOn, so TaskList can filter without checking task types. An event
counts on every day from its start date to its end date, so a
multi-day event shows up on each day it spans. The command takes a date
without a time, since it asks about a whole day, and it does not change
the task list, so nothing is saved.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #1 from SwaggyDaddy67/branch-Level-8
commitResults.messageBody: Level-8: Understand dates and times

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Finding a task means reading through the whole list, which gets slow
as the list grows.

Let's add "find KEYWORD", which lists every task whose description
contains the keyword, numbered from 1, or says that nothing matched.

Upper and lower case are ignored, since users rarely remember how they
capitalized a task. The keyword is everything after the command word,
so it may contain spaces, e.g. "find return book". Only descriptions
are searched; the on command already covers searching by date.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #2 from SwaggyDaddy67/branch-Level-9
commitResults.messageBody: Level-9: Find tasks by keyword

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc comments to the remaining members
commitResults.messageBody:
The toString overrides, Task.getDescription, the protected task fields,
two private Ui helpers, and several private fields have no header
comment, and Parser and Ui rely on undocumented default constructors.

Let's add a JavaDoc comment to each, and give Parser and Ui explicit
documented constructors.

Every class, method, and field now has a header comment. Parser's
constructor is private since all its methods are static, so it is
never meant to be created. The Ui constructor now creates the Scanner
that was set up in the field declaration. Behavior is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #3 from SwaggyDaddy67/branch-A-JavaDoc
commitResults.messageBody: A-JavaDoc: Add JavaDoc comments

commitResults.messageTitle: Say goodbye instead of crashing when input ends
commitResults.messageBody:
GLaDOS reads commands until it sees "bye". If the input ends first,
e.g. the user presses Ctrl+D, or commands are read from a file with no
"bye", reading the next line throws an exception and GLaDOS crashes
with a stack trace.

Let's check that another line exists before reading it, and treat the
end of input like the exit command.

GLaDOS then always shows its goodbye message and exits normally. Tasks
are already saved after every change, so nothing is lost.

commitResults.messageTitle: test-ui: Support data files in other encodings
commitResults.messageBody:
Allow a test to write its starting data file as Windows-1252 or as
UTF-8 with a byte order mark, instead of plain UTF-8.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep readable tasks when save file has bad bytes
commitResults.messageBody:
GLaDOS reads the data file as strict UTF-8. If any byte is not valid
UTF-8, e.g. "café" in a file saved by an older Windows editor, the
whole file is rejected and GLaDOS starts empty, so the next save
deletes every task. A file saved as "UTF-8 with BOM" also loses its
first task, as the invisible mark at the start makes that line
unreadable.

Let's decode the file leniently, so a bad byte only damages its own
line, skip lines containing such damaged characters as corrupted, and
remove a byte order mark from the start of the file.

Damaged lines are then reported and dropped like any other corrupted
line, as the user guide describes, and every other task is kept.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'fix-input-and-save-bugs'
Write the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
docs/README.md is still the template, with placeholder sections such
as "Feature ABC", so a user has no guide to the commands.

Let's replace it with a user guide covering setup, every command, the
accepted date and time forms, saving and editing the data file, known
issues, and a command summary, with screenshots of GLaDOS in use.

Each command follows the template's layout, and the Features section
follows the AddressBook-Level3 user guide. Every sample output was
copied from a real run, so the guide matches what GLaDOS prints.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-UserGuide'
Fix how the user guide displays on GitHub Pages
commitResults.messageBody:
On the published page, the data file's field separator shows as raw
backticks, since GitHub Pages does not render a code span with spaces
inside it. The page also starts with a large "ip" heading, as the site
title defaults to the repository name.

Let's describe the separator without spaces inside the code span, and
set the site title to GLaDOS in a GitHub Pages config file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'fix-user-guide-display'
